title: Edge minimal CP offline deploy checklist (annotated)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, field-friendly runbook for bootstrapping the minimal viable private control plane (CP) in an offline/airgapped edge site or restricted VPC. Focus: get a small CP up, validate model serving pathing, and provide safe, fast rollback/scale and upgrade primitives.

Scope and intent:
- Minimal: 1-3 control plane nodes + 1 seed-worker for verification. Not a full production cluster, but sufficient to validate deployments, certs, routing, and telemetry in constrained networks.
- Offline/artifact bundle approach: all docker images, kernels, TF modules, binary releases pre-bundled onto an external USB or internal package registry mirror.
- Terraform-driven provisioning where possible; small local scripts fill gaps (certs, local-CA, image import).

Assumptions / constraints:
- No external internet egress from the edge site except approved package mirror or staging bastion (explicitly allowed during bootstrap window).
- Customer provides L2/L3 network, IP ranges, and basic firewall ACL rules.
- Hardware: 3x control-plane-capable nodes (16-32GB RAM, 2+ cores), 1 small GPU worker for verification if required.
- KMS: Hardware KMS not required for minimal boot; integration steps included but optional.

Preflight checklist (quick):
- [ ] Rack/cabinet space, power + IP addresses allocated (management and dataplane networks)
- [ ] SSH keypairs provisioned (ops/cp-admin) and accessible
- [ ] Time sync verified (chrony/ntpd config file in bundle)
- [ ] Artifact bundle received: images.tar (all CP images), tarball of terraform modules, cert-tool binary, example env files
- [ ] Local container runtime installed (containerd recommended)
- [ ] Local image cache path mounted and writable (/var/lib/infra-cache)

Network & firewall quick reference (edge minimal):
- Management network (mgmt): nodes, operator laptop: full TCP/22 allowed
- Control plane API port: TCP 8443 (adjustable)
- Internal gRPC/eventing: TCP 50051-50060 (check module config)
- KV / datastore (etcd by default): TCP 2379-2380 between CP nodes only
- Metrics/telemetry ingestion (optional): TCP 9090 / 9100 (Prometheus push/pull rules differ)
- DNS: local DNS must resolve cluster service domain. If no DNS, add /etc/hosts entries during bootstrap.

Kernel / OS tweaks (notes):
- sysctl recommended: net.ipv4.ip_forward=1, vm.max_map_count=262144, fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288
- File descriptors: set ulimit -n >= 65536 for infra processes
- Transparent huge pages: disable (echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled)
- Ensure overlay/aufs module available for container runtime

Offline artifact handling (step-by-step):
1. Mount artifact bundle on a staging machine inside the site (sha256 checksum verify).
2. Load images locally: ctr -n k8s.io images import ./images.tar (containerd) or docker load -i images.tar
3. Populate internal registry (if present): tag and push: local-reg:5000/redwood/cp:1.2.3
4. Place terraform modules in /opt/tf-mods and set TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR to that path for faster operations

Terraform strategy and gotchas (field notes):
- Use local backend for initial bootstraps (state file kept on operator laptop and copied into site vault afterwards). Remote backends require network services that might not exist yet.
- Keep sensitive values out of tfvars checked into the bundle. Use tfvars.example and fill on-the-spot. We prefer a small script to inject secrets from operator environment into the run.
- Avoid modules that attempt to create cloud provider resources by default. Replace with edge-friendly stubs in the bundle (module-edge-networking).
- Use the following pattern for idempotent tagging: tag = "edge-{{local.site_id}}-{{timestamp}}" to avoid accidental collisions when reapplying.

Example minimal terraform invocation (local state):
- export TF_WORKING_DIR=/opt/tf-edge
- terraform init -backend=false ./modules/edge-cp
- terraform plan -var-file=site.tfvars -out=plan.out
- terraform apply plan.out

Bootstrap sequence (recommended order):
A. Node prep on each host (parallel where safe):
   - Install containerd, ntp/chrony, kernel tweaks, create infra user
   - Ensure /var/lib/infra-cache has images and artifact bundle extracted
   - Import CA certs into system store (if using customer CA)

B. Provision network interfaces & firewall rules via tf (or manual if network team handles it)

C. Provision etcd (if using builtin):
   - Start etcd on nodes with static peers config (IP-based).
   - Verify quorum: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints https://IP:2379 member list --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.pem --cert=/etc/etcd/cert.pem --key=/etc/etcd/key.pem
   - If etcd fails, collect /var/log/etcd/*.log before retrying.

D. Start control plane services (API, auth, registry shim):
   - Start in single-node mode for first node, then join others gradually.
   - Health-check endpoints built-in: /healthz and /ready, wait for both green.

E. Deploy seed-worker and run smoke tests (must be non-gpu):
   - Smoke tests: brief generation request, embeddings query, KV store write/read to verify routing.

Verification commands (field utils):
- curl -k https://<cp-api>:8443/healthz
- journalctl -u redwood-cp -f --no-pager (watch logs)
- /usr/local/bin/cpctl status --format short
- tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 8443 or port 2379 to inspect traffic pathing

Telemetry & logging (minimal footprint mode):
- Disable high-cardinality traces: set TRACING_SAMPLING=0.05 in env for initial boot
- Use local buffering: disk-based buffering path /var/lib/cp-buffer so logs are not lost during transient network issues
- If offline, configure push-to-collector window and set collector endpoint to local-relay:9100

Upgrade/rotation plan (safe minimal flows):
- Always take snapshot of etcd and copy to external USB before any control plane binary upgrades:
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.pem --cert=/etc/etcd/cert.pem --key=/etc/etcd/key.pem
- Upgrade sequence (single-node minimal):
  1) Quiesce non-essential services (disable autoscaling hooks)
  2) Verify healthy etcd snapshot and cluster health
  3) Drain node (if multi-node): cpctl node drain <node>
  4) Stop control plane service, replace binary/container image, start with --migrate-schema=false unless major version requires migration
  5) Run smoke tests, wait 5m, promote back to active
- For rotation of keys/certs: create new certs signed by customer CA or local CA, add to trust store, perform in-place reload where supported to avoid rolling restarts. If reload not supported, follow single-node upgrade pattern.

Rollback primitives (fast):
- If new binary/image fails sanity checks: revert image tag to previous stable tag and restart service.
- If etcd corrupted: restore from last snapshot (restore onto a clean cluster node per etcd restore docs). Maintain at least two snapshots on two separate devices.

Troubleshooting quick tips (ops notes):
- If API fails to start: check for port collision (systemd socket), missing CA path, or corrupted /var/lib/cp/meta/* files
- If nodes cannot join: inspect /etc/hosts and service CIDR overlaps; on edge sites this is common due to pre-existing NAT rules
- If telemetry backpressure observed: increase buffer size or reduce sampling temporarily

Operator shortcuts & helper scripts (put in bundle):
- import_images.sh (containerd/dockerd aware)
- tf-local-init.sh (creates local state dir and minimal tfvars from template)
- make-cert.sh (wraps openssl to produce customer CA signed artifacts)
- cp-health.sh (aggregates /healthz, logs, disk usage into single output)

Security notes (must read):
- Keep private CA keys off-site. Use a short-lived signing key for edge signing, rotate after onboarding.
- Avoid embedding secrets into terraform state; store encryption keys in on-prem vault and reference them via local secrets injection script.

Open questions / TODOs (field):
- TODO: formalize minimal metrics set and wire into local-relay config (Lena)
- TODO: test KMS shim with HSM simulator in an entirely offline environment (Ravi)
- Question: should we ship a tiny http-based artifact server as fallback for very small sites? Pros: cheaper than full registry; Cons: image pulling complexity.

Post-deploy checklist (first 24h):
- [ ] Verify cpu/mem usage of CP services < 70% on each node
- [ ] Confirm etcd compaction runs and disk usage stable
- [ ] Confirm telemetry derivative dashboards show expected small traffic pulses from smoke tests
- [ ] Record final artifact tags and state snapshots into site-runbook.txt and push to central repo when back online

Field notes (voice-of-operator):
- "If the site ops team insists on local DNS overrides, get their explicit /etc/hosts dump. We had a failure where service.domain -> internal loadbalancer IP was wrong and auth drifted."
- "During a dry-run in lab, replayed image-import failures: ensure containerd version >= 1.6.0 to avoid cross-architecture layer issue."

Appendix: minimal tfvars example (annotated)
-- site.tfvars --
site_id = "edge-nyc-rack22"
mgmt_cidr = "10.10.22.0/24"
control_plane_ips = ["10.10.22.10", "10.10.22.11"]
artifact_bundle_path = "/mnt/bundle-2025-01-10"
et_local_registry = "local-reg:5000"
use_etcd = true
etcd_snapshot_path = "/var/backups/etcd"

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally terse and operational — keep it near the operator laptop and in the site runbook.
- After initial run, convert recurring steps into guarded terraform modules and automate snapshot copy to offsite vault during network windows.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-14: initial draft (Ava)
- 2025-01-21: added terraform gotchas and example tfvars (Ravi)
- 2025-02-03: telemetry suggestions and rollback primitives added (Lena)
